Summary: "Remote karst valley located at the footstep of the Northeast Mountain range, the Đông Bắc, 100km from Hanoi in rural and traditional area." Description: "Quality sport routes dispatched on 17 crags within a radius of 5km. Most represented grades are in a solid 6b-7c range... All equipped in Inox 316." Access issues: "Tolerated. Most of the cliffs are located in private orchards... Most landlords might ask for access fees, usually VND 20,000-25,000. Bring exact change. It is a 40 minutes drive out of the valley (busy road, sketchy by bike) to an ATM." Approach: about 2 h from Hanoi by motorbike or private car

by public bus about 4 h via Gia Lam station for Lang Son, get down at Yen Vuong, taxi to Yen Thinh commune, requires Vietnamese. "Or VietClimb can help you get a public shuttle bus". Where to stay: "Mão's Homestay and Duc's bungalows, located from 1 to 5km from the crags, have been the main climbers' meeting point. They are community-based projects created and funded by VietClimb in 2018 and 2020." Ethic: "All local access with orchards' owners, Commune, District and Province authorities arranged by VietClimb." Gear: 15 draws usually not enough, need ~20, 25 for the longest, 30 if two routes at once. "Grades are (mostly) pretty accurate. theCrag Cat Ba Island 178 routes in crag, "Mostly Sport climbing", FR, 48 photos, 8,028 ascents. Grade histogram from 3a to 9a. Description: "more than 120 sport climbing routes on 13 crags, from 4a to 8a on Cat Ba Island and the beaches of Ha Long Bay. More than 230 deep water solo lines on 24 cliffs, from 4a to 7c+... If you are an independent climber you can explore the crags of the main island Cat Ba on your own, you just need a motorbike or bicycle." When to go: "The winter months are ideal for sport climbing, when the temperatures are cool (10-20 degrees celcius) and there is only moderate precipitation (5-25 mm a month). The downside of the winter are the unfavorable tides, which make DWS less enjoyable and only occasionally possible. A tide of over 2 meters is necessary to safely DWS in the bay". "The ideal time ... are the spring (April - May) and autumn months (September - November)... generally over 15 days a month where you can DWS." Access issues: "Rock Climbing in this area is more tolerated than actually allowed... Apart from needing passes from the local climbing companies, or paying a small fee to the local land owners upon arrival to climb, there is no other large access issues on land."
